ranked.headline: Learned and benchmarked models integrate single-cell and spatial omics across platforms
ranked.summary: Systematic benchmarks now quantify method performance, with spatial gene detection showing accuracy drops and false discoveries under realistic simulation.

ranked.headline: Learned models disentangle cell identity and state across single-cell and spatial data
ranked.summary: Atlas-scale single-cell and spatial multi-omics datasets now motivate multimodal, interpretable integration and annotation models.

ranked.headline: Compositional and error-model choices reshape omics testing and prediction
ranked.summary: Recent items recast zero handling, scale misspecification and feature representation as modeling decisions rather than preprocessing.

ranked.headline: ML and physics-based models prioritize ligands and binders before experimental testing
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair experimentally validated AI hit prioritization with blind head-to-head benchmarking of deep learning and classical models.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models recover regulatory and cell-state structure from omics data
ranked.summary: Foundation-scale pretraining and interpretable multimodal architectures are now applied to single-cell, methylation and cancer omics data.

ranked.headline: Isotope-labeling platforms IMPACT and 13CFLUX extend 13C metabolic flux analysis
ranked.summary: Stable-isotope flux tools now span untargeted-to-targeted metabolomics and stationary and nonstationary 13C analysis in one December 2025 batch.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked software tools for large-scale sequence and molecular library analysis
ranked.summary: Parameter guidance and benchmarking now target scalability and accuracy in routine bioinformatics pipelines.

ranked.headline: Alignment-free and index-based methods advance variant and repeat detection from reads
ranked.summary: Recent work applies k-mer pseudo-mapping, run-length PBWT indexing, and tokenization to variant and repeat detection from sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Computational models link single-cell and spatial omics data to interpretable mechanisms
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell datasets are now analyzed with physics-informed, graph-based, and statistically constrained models.

ranked.headline: Truth-anchored benchmarks expose variability in structural and small variant calling
ranked.summary: Reference-anchored benchmarks now span structural variants, targeted NGS, and genome truth sets, exposing pipeline-dependent sensitivity and error rates.

ranked.headline: Testing whether genomic deep learning predictions are valid, not merely accurate
ranked.summary: Deep learning predictors for splicing, variant effects, and protein design are being audited for confounders, leakage, missingness, and robustness.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based deep learning for TCR, MHC, B cell and antibody recognition
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications benchmark and extend sequence-based models of TCR-pMHC binding, T cell immunogenicity and antibody maturation.

ranked.headline: Stability and criticality constrain neural dynamics from single neurons to whole brain
ranked.summary: Unified and theory-neutral frameworks now link excitability, circuit stability, and whole-brain criticality as constraints on observed neural dynamics.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics evidence is being integrated to annotate and prioritize candidate genes
ranked.summary: Genetic, regulatory, and network data are now combined in scalable, searchable resources for gene-level annotation and candidate prioritization.

ranked.headline: Learned models decode RNA and chromatin regulation from sequence and epigenomic data
ranked.summary: Probabilistic and transformer models now extract RNA processing and chromatin compartment information from routine sequencing and epigenomic data.

ranked.headline: Decomposing multi-omic and sequencing data into technical and phenotypic components
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs phenotype-aligned embeddings and supervised factorization with multi-omic microbiome and plant data to isolate biological signal.

ranked.headline: Structure-aware models for protein binding, affinity, and mutation pathogenicity
ranked.summary: Predicted structures now serve as training substrates for biomolecular models spanning docking, design, affinity, and mutation effects.

ranked.headline: Standardized workflows and curated references for microbial metagenomic profiling
ranked.summary: Automated prophage, mycobiome, and cross-domain profiling tools now package manual metagenomic analyses into reproducible, curated workflows and reference…

ranked.headline: Language models and graph learners predict drug and omics-linked molecular responses
ranked.summary: Pretrained language models and graph transformers now extend omics and drug-association prediction to metabolomic risk, perturbation and microbial data.

ranked.headline: New statistical methods extend GWAS to multivariate traits, missing data and haplotypes
ranked.summary: Recent work targets GWAS limitations: missing genotypes in meta-analysis, multivariate effect estimation, and haplotype definition.

ranked.headline: Standalone and web tools standardize and integrate heterogeneous biomolecular records
ranked.summary: Recent December 2025 releases offer web and standalone tools for canonicalizing, analyzing, and visualizing structured biomolecular and cryoEM archive data.

ranked.headline: Statistical inference links within-host and population pathogen dynamics to forecasts
ranked.summary: Recent studies apply scalable Bayesian inference and unsupervised fitness estimation to viral surveillance and vaccine strain forecasting.

ranked.headline: Telomere-to-telomere insect genomes and protein-DNA language models score plant variants
ranked.summary: Recent T2T assemblies of two dipterans and new language-model variant scoring in maize extend reference quality and functional prediction.

ranked.headline: Scaling Bayesian inference for stochastic reaction networks and microbial dynamics
ranked.summary: Simulation, neural estimation, and identifiability workflows now target inference cost and reliability directly within the mechanistic model.

ranked.headline: Spatial single-cell data constraining physics-based models of tumor and tissue dynamics
ranked.summary: Spatial transcriptomics and live imaging now feed mechanistic simulations, moving inference beyond correlation between cell states and tissue features.

ranked.headline: Interpretable computational frameworks for neuroimaging and multimodal brain biomarkers
ranked.summary: Interpretability, replicability, and longitudinal or dynamic brain representations are explicit emphases in recent neuroimaging biomarker methods.

ranked.headline: Graph-based methods reconstruct polyploid and diploid haplotypes from sequencing reads
ranked.summary: Recent work adds uncertainty quantification, alignment-free pangenome genotyping, and deep reinforcement learning to read-based haplotype assembly.

ranked.headline: Learned and Bayesian models refine genetic association variant prioritization
ranked.summary: Recent work applies deep learning, Bayesian aggregation and shrinkage to improve association discovery at both variant and gene levels.

ranked.headline: Compact indexes and embeddings speed up searching and classifying sequences at scale
ranked.summary: Compact indexes and word embeddings are applied to plasmid, 16S, barcode, and fungal mobile element data to make large sequence collections searchable.

ranked.headline: Re-implemented transcript quantification tools for single-cell and long-read RNA-seq
ranked.summary: Preprints and a published tool extend pseudoalignment and barcode-correction workflows to new transcriptome data types at varied scales.

ranked.headline: Long-read references expose complex loci and ancestry bias in gene annotation
ranked.summary: Long-read sequencing now resolves MHC and tandem-repeat loci, but cross-ancestry annotation gaps persist in human and mouse references.

ranked.headline: Methods sample protein conformational ensembles and pathways beyond single structures
ranked.summary: Diffusion sampling, cryo-EM ensemble fitting, and B-factor decoding now target conformational heterogeneity rather than single structures.

ranked.headline: Geometry-driven computational design of enzyme active sites and substrate prediction
ranked.summary: Atom-level scaffolding and geometry-based descriptors now let computational pipelines target catalytic arrays and substrate fit directly.

ranked.headline: Deep networks link imaging and histology inputs to somatic mutations and diagnoses
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs foundation-model and graph encoders with imaging, genomic, and clinical data to predict mutation status and disease classes.

ranked.headline: Sequence mining sets jingmenvirus benchmarks and shows plasmids diversify T6SS
ranked.summary: Expanding mined sequence collections now support explicit taxonomic thresholds and plasmid-level analysis of secretion system diversity.

ranked.headline: Web tools integrate omics and machine learning to nominate biomarker panels and drug…
ranked.summary: Recent publications describe open web platforms that apply machine learning to multi-omics and network data for biomarker and drug target prioritization.

ranked.headline: Embedding privacy into genomic association, synthetic generation, and haplotype phasing
ranked.summary: Late-2025 papers embed formal privacy guarantees into association, synthetic genome, and phasing analyses of individual-level data.

ranked.headline: Algorithms infer active X chromosome, karyotypes and single-cell lineage trees
ranked.summary: Recent methods extract active X status, optical-map karyotypes and genotype-resolved lineage trees directly from single-cell and optical mapping data.

ranked.headline: MD simulations reveal how peptide, ligand and glycan binding reshape protein conformation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply all-atom and steered MD to peptide-MHC, GPCR and glycosylated receptor systems in parallel.

ranked.headline: Computational resolution of proteoforms, molecular variants, and protein fold switching
ranked.summary: Scaling sequence, mass spectra, and predicted structures into integrated computational evidence layers now enables proteome- and library-wide analysis.
